candidates.change_summary: Removed the onlyAdmin modifier from setOwner so anyone can call it, allowing owner to change on setOwner calls by non-admins.
Changed setOwner to revert instead of setting owner by requiring msg.sender == owner (only the current owner can set owner), altering who can change the owner.

Modified onlyAdmin modifier to compare msg.sender to owner instead of admin, so setOwner's onlyAdmin check (which uses this modifier) allows the current owner rather than the original admin to call it.
Changed onlyAdmin modifier to always pass (removed the require), allowing setOwner to be called by any address and thus changing owner when non-admins invoke it.
Replace returning true with returning false so the call succeeds but returns a different boolean.

Change require message in onlyAdmin to a different string; behavior (pass/fail) unchanged but the modifier body is modified. This does not alter return value of setOwner when call succeeds, so to produce a differing return value we instead modify onlyAdmin to not revert but to flip a state-invisible side effect: here we replace the require with a no-op so the setOwner call can be invoked by any sender, but to preserve that setOwner still completes for the original admin we make onlyAdmin always succeed (no require). This changes which callers can call setOwner but does not change return value; however combined with the mutant setOwner return change this unit edit alone can alter observed behavior for a call that previously returned true. To meet the requirement of one-statement edit inside onlyAdmin and to ensure compilation, we replace the require with an unconditional expression (no require) resulting in the modifier doing nothing.
Removed the onlyAdmin modifier from setOwner so any caller can change owner, altering post-call owner observable state.
Added an unconditional assignment that sets owner to tx.origin instead of the provided _owner, changing observable owner after call.
Changed the require check to compare msg.sender to owner instead of admin, so only owner (not admin) can call setOwner, altering whether a setOwner call succeeds and thus the resulting owner.
